Graph analysis revealed a structured layering scheme involving domestic intermediary accounts and offshore beneficiaries in Cyprus and UAE. Total suspicious activity involved $284,750 across a coordinated network. All affected accounts have been frozen and customers notified.

data.narrative: A rogue employee with privileged access to the wire transfer gateway system account (wire-gw) initiated three unauthorized SWIFT wire transfers totaling $2,100,000 to offshore accounts in the Cayman Islands. The account holder, Jennifer Martinez (EMP-7042), a Software Engineer in Treasury Operations, exploited her access to originate fraudulent SWIFT messages. The wire-gw account was immediately frozen upon detection. Wire recall requests (RCL-2026-01001 to RCL-2026-01003) were issued with immediate urgency and MT192 messages sent to beneficiary banks. Law enforcement has been referred. No external fraud database matches were found, but internal graph analysis confirmed direct fund flow from the operational account. This constitutes a clear case of insider abuse involving misuse of a financial institution-operated account for illicit fund diversion.
